key_insight: AI-guided single-cell morphology and label-free enrichment revealed phenotypic diversity, shared genomic alterations, and genomic divergence in metastatic breast cancer effusions.
clinical_relevance: Malignant effusions may provide accessible material for research into metastatic tumor heterogeneity, although clinical utility and drug-discovery impact remain unproven.
method: Apply a pretrained deep-learning model to single-cell brightfield images to estimate tumor and immune-cell fractions.
Use morphology-guided microfluidics to enrich putative tumor cells without labeling.
Profile copy-number alterations and mutations, comparing enriched cells with available matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors.
evidence_signal: In 10 patients, AI identified putative tumor cells across 25 samples (median tumor fraction: 5.4%); immune-cell estimates correlated with flow cytometry (r = 0.69–0.75), and unsupervised analysis identified four tumor morphotypes.
watch_item: The small cohort limits generalizability, and low tumor fractions can weaken genomic signals; morphology-based identification requires orthogonal validation.
paper_title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions
